sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yaakov, as the central line, is like a rope connecting the highest and lowest levels, and through teshuvah, even in the desolate wilderness, God finds him and raises him above Torah and mitzvos.

translations.translation: And this is, "As an eagle stirs up its nest," etc.,

which refers to what precedes it: "For the portion of Hashem is His people, Yaakov the lot of His inheritance; He found him in a desert land," etc., "He encircled him, He cared for him, as the apple of His eye."
Yaakov is the aspect of the central line, as above,
therefore he is equal from his beginning to his end.
For this is "Yaakov the lot of His inheritance," which is analogous to a rope, one end of which is above and the other end below,
so that when one moves its lower end, its upper end also moves, as explained in Igeres HaTeshuvah,
because since Yaakov is the central line, therefore he is "the lot of His inheritance," etc.
"He found him in a desert land,"
"Desert" is where no man dwells,
meaning that the aspect of the Supernal Man, which is drawn down through Torah and mitzvos, does not dwell there.
Nevertheless, through teshuvah,
(the central line)
"He found him in a desert land and in a desolate, howling wilderness,"
that even there He finds him,
as explained in Likkutei Torah
regarding the matter of "And you shall seek from there."
"He encircled him, He cared for him, as the apple of His eye"
is the black of the eye from which the light emerges, as Rashi explains,
and this is the matter of
"the transformation of darkness into light,"
for when one transforms darkness into light, then there is the advantage of light,
as is known
regarding the matter of "the advantage of light from darkness."
And upon this, it continues afterward: "As an eagle stirs up its nest," etc., "He carries it on His pinions," that from the aspect of the eagle, which is the aspect of Atik, as above,
(for there the central line reaches?)
"He carries it on His pinions,"
above Torah and mitzvos,
so that even one who was deficient in his service, and even one who sinned and transgressed and strayed from the path,
there is drawn for him pardon, forgiveness, and atonement,
and even that there is drawn for him from the aspect that is above Torah and mitzvos,
"on His pinions,"
and it concludes: "Hashem alone shall lead him, and there is no alien god with Him,"
"that no stranger may share with you, and they shall be yours alone,"
Israel and the King alone.
